title: AI Fashion Product Photography: Studio or Lifestyle First?
author: SetlesStudio Team
excerpt: One outfit, eight images. See which photo shows the side tie, which sells the quilted bag, and which belongs in a collection launch email.
metaTitle: AI Fashion Product Photography: Studio or Lifestyle First?
metaDescription: Compare studio and lifestyle AI fashion product photography using one burgundy outfit. Choose the first product photo, campaign scene and mobile crop.
body:
There’s a little bow at the hip of this burgundy top. In one picture, you can follow both ends of the tie against the white skirt. In another, a quilted bag sits right over it. Both pictures belong in the collection. Only one would be my first choice for selling the top. For this top, I’d lead the product page with the studio portrait where the model holds the bag down by her knee. For the collection email, I’d open with the flower shop. Here’s how we’d use one outfit across a launch, and what to look for when you commission AI fashion and product photography for your own store. ## Selling the burgundy top? Keep the side tie in view Take a look at the original flat lay beside the AI studio image. On the left, the top, skirt and bag share the frame. You can trace the curve of the burgundy hem and see exactly where the white pleats begin. On the right, the bag hangs down by the model’s knee. Moving it that small distance clears the waist. Now you can see how the gathered side lifts the hem when the outfit is worn.
Original product reference. Look for the two loose ends of the tie.
Studio view. Lowering the bag makes the outline of the top easier to read. For a listing that sells the top on its own, I’d lead with the second image and frame it from the shoulders to just below the ties. Keep the full-length version next in the gallery for the shopper who wants styling ideas. If the skirt and bag are sold separately, say so beside the photo. ## Selling the bag? Show its depth as well as its clasp Compare the two shoulder-bag poses below. In one, you see the quilted flap and clasp. In the other, the bag turns sideways and you can judge its depth against the model’s arm. If the handbag is your product, that pair earns its place. If the top is your product, one is enough. Use the spare gallery slot for a real close-up of the ruching or a back view.
Face of the bag visible. A useful angle for showing the flap and hardware.
Side of the bag visible. The change of angle shows its profile. Before approving AI product photography, open the generated shot beside the original and zoom in on the detail a customer is paying for. Here I’d check the drawstring, the spacing of the pleats and the clasp. If the handbag is the item for sale, send a separate photograph of its hardware. A full-outfit reference gives the clasp only a handful of pixels. ## The flower shop or the green doorway? Choose a scene for the launch I’d pick the flower shop. The pink blossoms sit just behind the model’s shoulder, and the pale skirt is easy to follow against the darker shopfront. It gives a spring collection email a setting before the reader gets to the first sentence.
Campaign opener. The flowers give this outfit a season and an occasion. For a quieter lookbook, I’d pick the green doorway. Compare the two frames. In the first, the model faces you and the skirt falls almost straight. In the second, one foot steps forward and the bag swings into view. That second frame would be my pick for an accessories feature. The bag is also exactly what makes it a weaker choice for explaining the side tie.
Front-facing doorway view for the full look.
Three-quarter doorway view for an accessories feature. ## Where does the model go when the banner hits a phone?
Desktop banner. The left side has room for a collection name and a shop button. Try squeezing this wide image into a narrow phone screen. A center crop can lose the model entirely. Give your designer the wide banner for desktop and a portrait studio frame for mobile. You already have both shapes in this set. ## Book a studio set, a lifestyle campaign, or both If your next deadline is a product-page launch, start with SetlesStudio’s AI studio photography for clothing brands. Tell us which item is for sale and which detail needs to be visible in the first image. If your product page is ready and you have a collection to announce, choose AI lifestyle fashion photography. Send the outfit and tell us where the image will run. A portrait for an email and a wide homepage banner call for different framing. Have a flat lay ready? Send it with one sentence: “We’re selling ___, and the first thing a shopper needs to see is ___.” We can plan your studio shots, your campaign images, or both around that answer.
